# `INU-8` — Resolve app-contributed inbox sources through the app registry's manifest factory (InboxTypeHandler) + make the PROVIDER_TYPES/handler guard bidirectional

## Intent — what this is for

Provider-seam contract change owned by this plan (the inbox source seam). Closes the declarable-but-unhandled gap for `inbox` and repairs the one-directional #47 guard. Unblocks CE-8 part 1 (Slack inbox source) and EIAT-2 (mail-inbox provider), whose app-side adapters are already written and inert.

## Done when

An app declaring {"type":"inbox","implementation":"mod:factory"} in app.json has its provider resolved and registered at enable-time by a real InboxTypeHandler (registered via register_type_handler("inbox", ...), the same load_factory path every other app provider type uses) and DEREGISTERED on disable/uninstall so no phantom source survives; inbox_providers.get_default_provider(name) resolves app-contributed sources with a documented precedence (app-registry factory -> entry-point group -> native -> filesystem) and its SEAM LIMIT docstring is replaced by the real contract; the class-vs-instance shape mismatch is handled explicitly (entry points yield a CLASS, a manifest factory yields an INSTANCE) rather than by duck-typing at the call site; a fixture app's inbox source is driven end-to-end (declare -> enable -> messages flow through the generic seam -> disable -> source gone); test_provider_types_equal_registered_handlers asserts BOTH directions with an explicit reason-carrying allowlist, and each of the three remaining unhandled types (agent, notification, skills) is resolved per type: given a handler, or removed from PROVIDER_TYPES, or allowlisted with the mechanism that actually serves it named in the reason (skills ship via apps/skill_seed.py, not a provider) — no type is left silently declarable-and-dead
